Wittgenstein holds two views of language, also known as Early Wittgenstein and Late Wittgenstein.

In the _Tractatus_, a sentence is a picture of a fact: it means something because its parts are arranged the way the parts of the world are. The embed below is from this period.
In Philosophical Investigations, A word’s meaning is its use inside a “language-game”, and no more “picture” concept— a shared activity with rules, such as giving orders, describing an object or telling a joke. He also warns that “a picture held us captive” (§115): one model of how language must work can stop us from looking at how it does work.
My reading: conflict starts when two people play different games with the same words and each assumes the other plays theirs. Online, where one sentence reaches many audiences at once, this shows up as context collapse.

Possibly the most salient feature of LLMs is that the system is surprisingly patient in each interaction with humans.

representations
A language model is one compressed representation of a large corpus of human text. It learns which continuations of a text are likely, so whatever knowledge it holds, it holds through the way people have written.
Deep learning rose to prominence because it learns its features from data, in place of features that people design by hand. Whether those learned features resemble how we perceive the world is an open question, and part of what representation research asks.
